evidence: The proposed reproduction breaks at the mixed-version connection premise. The settled artifact requires the redesigned canonical store to assign every new ACK-required ordinary send a send-time deadline (root Message deadline contract), and ht-0lo.1.1 owns that projection; ht-0lo.1.3 owns upgrading the legacy store. It does not state that a modern CLI must obtain redesigned ordinary-send semantics from an unupgraded daemon, or that existing protocol/version negotiation permits that client-daemon combination. Its explicit new compatibility obligation is narrower: negotiate before mutations requiring the new invitation representation, with subtree validation likewise mentioning new incompatible fields. A wire-compatible ordinary send to an older daemon retaining older behavior is therefore a hypothetical unsupported-version scenario, not an end-to-end contradiction demonstrated against the stated scope. The absence of a dedicated receipt capability or mixed-version receipt test alone does not establish a material gap; confirmation would require a stated mixed-version ordinary-send guarantee or evidence within the named artifact that supported negotiation admits the old daemon while promising the new timer behavior.
